title.narrative: Building Institutions And Systems to Harness And Realize Agenda 2063 Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda 2063 Project for Africa is to improve the capacity of the African Union Commission (AUC) and the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat in supporting member states to negotiate and implement selected commitments to enhance regional integration and intracontinental trade in Africa. The project comprises of three components. The first component, improved effectiveness of the AUC management functions will finance activities to continue the deepening of some activities initiated under the first project, and it will accelerate implementation of measures to strengthen the institutional capacity of the AUC to support Agenda 2063. It consists of following sub-components: (i) upgrading financial management, procurement, and oversight; (ii) innovations to improve human resource management; and (iii) improving functionality and performance of information and communication technologies (ICT) systems. The second component, improved capacity for implementation of commitments to enhance intracontinental trade and investment will finance activities to accelerate the deepening of measures to expand intracontinental trade and investment, liberalize air connectivity, and enhance the free movement of persons. It consists of following sub-components: (i) supporting the implementation of the AfCFTA treaty; (ii) supporting the implementation of the single Africa air transport market (SAATM); and (iii) supporting the implementation of the free movement of persons (FMP). The third component, project implementation, results-based management, and stakeholder engagement will support activities required to ensure the effective implementation of the project.

To improve the capacity of the African Union Commission and the African Continental Free Trade Area Secretariat in supporting member states to negotiate and implement selected commitments to enhance regional integration and intracontinental trade in Africa.

condition.narrative: (Section I.A. 3 Schedule 2)The Recipient shall establish, not later than sixty (60) days after the Effective Date, and thereaftermaintain, at all times during the implementation of the Project, a Steering Committee (the “Steering Committee”), chaired by theAUCDirector General and comprised of, inter alia, directors of participating department of the AUC and the AfCFTA Secretariat, withmandate, composition and resources acceptable to the Association, responsible for providing strategic guidance to Projectimplementation, including approval of the key performance indicators and the annual work plan and budget.

(Section I.B.1 Schedule 2) The Recipient shall adopt, not later than ninety (90) days after the Effective Date, and thereafterimplement the Project in accordance with a Project operations manual (“Project Operations Manual” or “POM”), acceptable to theAssociation, which shall include fiduciary policies and procedures to be followed by the Recipient in conducting its operations,including the Project, and such manual shall cover, inter alia, financial management, procurement, disbursement and monitoring andevaluation arrangements for the Project.

title.narrative: Operationalization of the AfCFTA Dispute Settlement Body

baseline.value: Core elements of the Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) not in place except Appellate Body.

target.value: AfCFTA Secretariat has conducted training on key elements of dispute resolution ( e.g., dispute settlement and the appeal process) to key stakeholders in another 15 State Parties.

comment.narrative: Measures establishment and functioning of the Dispute Settlement Body.

actual.value:
All core components of the DSM have been successfully established and are operational, with the exception of the Dispute Settlement Portal, which remains under development (The TOR for the development of the DS Portal has been finalized).
Capacity-building on dispute settlement for appellate body members and panelists conducted has reached 16 state parties . A peer learning and capacity building activity planned with The Southern Common Market (Mercosur) in January 2026

baseline.value: AUC IT systems functionality and processes are sub-optimal, architecture inadequate, and ICT Infrastructure is not fully integrated.

target.value: Completed upgrade of network infrastructure performance and security (Measurement: At least: i. Deployment of High Density Wireless Infrastructure; ii. Deployment of Access and Distribution Switches for NCC Building; iii. Deployment of a Network Access Control Soution on Compatible Network Access Switches; iv. Upgrade Network Analytics Solution, v. comment.narrative: Measures progress in improving the functionality and performance of AUC ICT infrastructure and tools.

actual.value:
The contracts for several key ICT initiatives at the African Union are in the process of being finalized and signed by the Acting Director of OSSD. These include the supply and delivery of IT equipment and ITSM tools to the AU Headquarters and Organs, the installation of networking and security solutions at the Headquarters, SAP ECC and HCM configurations, and the development of an ERP roadmap.
The MISD has already initiated procurement processes for network infrastructure and equipment, as well as Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions. Several contracts have been initiated for consultancies to start the preparatory activities for the new ERP to be started in January

title.narrative: Increased effectiveness of critical financial management processes of the AUC

baseline.value: The following functions are not in place: (a) multi-year planning and budgeting; (b) mid year budget review; (c) end to end automated payment system; and (d) compliance with financial reporting requirements.

target.value: The following are in place and functioning: a)multi-year planning and budgeting; (b) mid year budget review; (c) end to end automated payment system; and (d) compliance with financial reporting requirements.

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the extent to which AUC has achieved key milestones in improving financial management systems, policies, and practices to improve overall financial management quality at the AUC. For end to end automation means that Communications regarding all transactions with Banks are done through SAP via SWIFT. Requires evidence of interface of bank and payment system and also reconciliation statements and payment logs generated from SWIFT. Statutory reports are (i) Annual consolidated Financial Statement of previous year (usually prepared by June 30) and (ii) Mid Term Review of current year/Budget Performance (usually prepared by end of August).

actual.value:
A) 3 year budget exists in principle but typically implemented per year. For it to be fully operational, it will be subject to approval by member states and in line with the recently approved 2024- 2028 AUC Strategy
B) Mid-Year Budget Performance Report covering January to June has been published
C) A contract has been signed to restart the implementation of the BCM. It covers testing and ‘go-live’ for the other banks- it should be completed in the first quarter of the 2026 An aggregated figure on compliance not available for 2025
